name: main
prose: Test program entry point of ioam6_parser.c (the slice showed only the tail of main, lines 1071-1101, and no function named unnamed_ioam6_hbh_layout_check exists). main(argc, argv) returns the unsigned int ret, initialised to 1, and returns 0 only when check_ioam_trace returns 0. Steps in order: if argc != 9 it returns 1; it maps argv[2] through str2id, parses argv[3] and argv[4] as IPv6 addresses (src, dst), argv[5] as a hex u32 (tr_type), argv[6] as u8 (tr_size) and argv[7] as u16 (ioam_ns), returning 1 on any failure; nexthdr is IPPROTO_IPV6 when argv[8] equals "encap" and IPPROTO_ICMPV6 otherwise; hoplen is sizeof(hbh) + 2 + sizeof(ioam6 header) + sizeof(trace header) + tr_size + (tr_size % 8). It opens an AF_PACKET/SOCK_DGRAM socket for ETH_P_IPV6, binds it to the device named in argv[1] with SO_BINDTODEVICE and sets a 1 second SO_RCVTIMEO; a failure of any of those calls returns 1 (after closing the socket once it exists). It then recv()s into a 512-byte buffer; a recv result <= 0 (including the timeout) returns 1 after closing. Packets whose IPv6 source or destination differ from src/dst, or whose nexthdr is not hop-by-hop, are skipped by receiving again. For the first matching packet it checks the hop-by-hop next header and hdrlen against nexthdr and (hoplen >> 3) - 1, the 2 padding bytes (the test is ptr[0] != IPV6_TLV_PADN && ptr[1] != 0, so it fails only when both are wrong), the IOAM option type, its opt_len and IOAM6_TYPE_PREALLOC, and, when tr_size % 8 is nonzero, the trailing padding bytes (a conjunction of four != tests, so it fails only when all four differ); any failing check jumps to close and returns 1. Finally ret = check_ioam_trace(testname_id, trace, tr_type, tr_size, ioam_ns), the socket is closed, and ret is returned (check_ioam_trace returns 1 on a header mismatch or when the test id is in neither range, otherwise the result of check_data). The header reads are not checked against the received size, only against the 512-byte buffer.
note: Slice cut the head; fixed under real name main (ioam6_parser.c:1002-1101). Old record said dropped; the fragment is the tail of main. No reviewer claim (mechanical rejection only).

name: build_packet_udp
prose: Static function build_packet_udp(_uh) in csum.c fills the UDP header at _uh from the cfg_* globals and returns a pointer just past the header (uh + 1). It sets source to htons(cfg_port_src), dest to htons(cfg_port_dst), len to htons(sizeof(struct udphdr) + cfg_payload_len) and check to 0. If cfg_zero_sum is set it sets source to 0, then to the value of checksum(uh, IPPROTO_UDP, sizeof(struct udphdr) + cfg_payload_len), prints the old and new source ports to stderr and stores ntohs(source) into cfg_port_src. Then check becomes 0 when cfg_zero_disable is set, otherwise checksum(uh, IPPROTO_UDP, sizeof(struct udphdr) + cfg_payload_len); if cfg_bad_csum is set the check value is then replaced by its bitwise complement (so with cfg_zero_disable and cfg_bad_csum both set it becomes 0xFFFF). It prints "tx: sending checksum: 0x%x" with the check value to stderr and returns uh + 1. The helper checksum() reads the pseudo-header addresses through the global iph_addr_p (8 bytes for PF_INET, 32 for PF_INET6, selected by cfg_family) and, when cfg_do_tx and cfg_send_pfpacket are both set, returns only the complemented folded pseudo-header sum without covering the UDP data; otherwise it sums the header and payload over len bytes. Preconditions: _uh points to a writable udphdr followed by cfg_payload_len payload bytes already in place, and iph_addr_p was set by the IP header builder. The buffer stays with the caller.
note: Reviewer claims: round 1 (cfg_bad_csum flips check even when cfg_zero_disable is set, so not 0) right (csum.c:249-250); round 1 (precondition omits iph_addr_p) right since checksum() uses it (csum.c:176); round 2 (annotation says void) wrong, function returns void * (csum.c:225,253); round 15 (claims a print of the final checksum but code has none) wrong, fprintf at csum.c:252. Also the old prose said checksum(uh,...) without qualification; in the PF_PACKET tx case it is pseudo-header only (csum.c:181-182). Tally 2 right 2 wrong.

name: recv_prepare_packet
prose: Static function recv_prepare_packet() takes no parameters and returns a file descriptor. It creates a socket(PF_PACKET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0), sets SO_RCVBUF to cfg_rcvbuf, enables PACKET_AUXDATA, calls recv_prepare_packet_filter(fd) and recv_prepare_packet_bind(fd), then returns fd. The filter is a classic BPF program attached with SO_ATTACH_FILTER that accepts a packet (returns 0xFFFF) only when the packet type is PACKET_HOST, the IP protocol/next-header byte equals IPPROTO_UDP when cfg_encap is set (otherwise cfg_proto), and the 16-bit destination port equals cfg_port_dst; cfg_family only selects whether those two offsets are taken from an IPv4 header (cfg_family == AF_INET) or an IPv6 header. The bind step sets sll_protocol to ETH_P_IP when cfg_family == PF_INET and ETH_P_IPV6 otherwise, resolves cfg_ifname with if_nametoindex and binds. If socket creation, either setsockopt (including the filter attach), if_nametoindex returning 0, or bind fails, error(1, ...) is called with a nonzero status, which terminates the process, so the function does not return in those cases. Globals read: cfg_rcvbuf, cfg_family, cfg_proto, cfg_encap, cfg_port_dst, cfg_ifname.
note: Reviewers: round 1 and round 2 (claims about an fd parameter / returning nothing) wrong, the function takes no argument and returns fd (csum.c:546-569) and the old prose already said so; round 15 (precondition omits cfg_proto/cfg_port_dst; filter checks protocol and port, not address family) right (csum.c:497-506, 515-525), rewritten. Tally 1 right 2 wrong.

name: copyfd_io_poll
prose: Static function copyfd_io_poll(infd, peerfd, outfd, in_closed_after_out, winfo) in mptcp_connect.c (lines 634-767; the packet slice began inside earlier functions). It puts peerfd into non-blocking mode (the fcntl result is ignored) and loops on poll() of peerfd for POLLIN|POLLOUT with poll_timeout. The loop exits and the function returns 0 (after usleep(cfg_wait) when cfg_remove is set and quit is not) when the event mask becomes 0 or the global quit is set, when a read of peerfd returns 0 while POLLOUT is already cleared (in that case *in_closed_after_out is set to true first), when reading infd returns 0 bytes while POLLIN is already cleared, or when cfg_truncate > 0 and both the total written and the total read have reached cfg_truncate. Other returns: 0 immediately (without the cfg_remove sleep) when a read from peerfd fails, with any errno, while cfg_rcv_trunc is set; 1 when poll() fails with errno other than EINTR (EINTR retries); 2 on poll timeout; 3 when reading peerfd fails and cfg_rcv_trunc is not set; 4 when reading infd fails with errno other than EINTR; 5 when revents has POLLERR or POLLNVAL and cfg_rcv_trunc is not set (when it is set the loop simply continues); 111 when do_rnd_write to peerfd fails, except that when cfg_rcv_trunc is set and errno is ECONNRESET or EPIPE, POLLOUT is cleared and the loop continues (so 111 is returned for any write failure when cfg_rcv_trunc is not set, and for other errnos when it is). Data movement: bytes read from peerfd are written to outfd with do_write (its result is ignored); bytes to send come from winfo->buf/off/len, refilled with read(infd, ...) when winfo->len is 0; when infd reaches EOF and POLLIN is still enabled it calls shut_wr(peerfd), which sleeps cfg_wait microseconds if set and then does shutdown(peerfd, SHUT_WR). peerfd is left non-blocking.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (returns 0 on read error when cfg_rcv_trunc, not only clean completion) right (mptcp_connect.c:689-691); round 15 (111 also when cfg_rcv_trunc is false) right (lines 714-724, the exception is conditioned on cfg_rcv_trunc). Tally 2 right 0 wrong. Slice began inside other functions; checked against the whole function.

name: client
prose: Static function client(pipefd) in mptcp_sockopt.c (lines 771-793; the packet slice began inside test_ip_tos_sockopt). It calls alarm(15), then, depending on the global pf, connects an MPTCP socket to 127.0.0.1:15432 (AF_INET) or ::1:15432 (AF_INET6) with sock_connect_mptcp(..., IPPROTO_MPTCP); any other pf calls xerror, which prints a message and calls exit(1). It then calls test_ip_tos_sockopt(fd) and connect_one_server(fd, pipefd) and returns 0. It has no other return statement, so it returns 0 whenever those calls return; sock_connect_mptcp, test_ip_tos_sockopt (die_perror/xerror, both of which exit(1)) and connect_one_server (die_perror/xerror, asserts) can end the process instead. Relevant behaviour of test_ip_tos_sockopt: it exits when setsockopt/getsockopt IP_TOS fail, when the value read back differs, when the returned length is not 1, when a getsockopt with length 0 fails or leaves a nonzero length, when the final getsockopt with length (socklen_t)-1 returns something other than -1 while errno is not EINVAL (die_perror), and when that length is changed from -1 (xerror); these checks are independent, and a final getsockopt returning -1 passes without errno being checked. connect_one_server closes fd and pipefd itself; client closes neither.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (formal requires weaker than prose) moot, no contract now; round 2 (test_ip_tos_sockopt can fail without terminating, r == -1 and errno != EINVAL, so client may return 0) right (mptcp_sockopt.c:765); round 15 (die_perror triggers on r != -1 && errno != EINVAL regardless of s; xerror on s != -1) right, and the old prose's nested 'only if s != -1' was wrong. Tally 2 right 0 wrong (1 moot).

name: do_server
prose: Static function do_server(args, ipc_fd) in nettest.c (lines 1562-1666). ipc_fd is -1 when there is no parent to signal (ipc_write then does nothing; otherwise it writes the int message to ipc_fd and only logs a failure). Steps: if args->serverns is set it calls switch_ns (failure logs and goes to err_exit); it sets args->dev = args->server_dev and args->expected_dev = args->expected_server_dev; resolve_devices or validate_addresses failing goes to err_exit; it uses a timeout of prog_timeout seconds when prog_timeout is nonzero; it creates the listening socket with msock_server when args->has_grp, otherwise lsock_init, and a negative result goes to err_exit. err_exit does ipc_write(ipc_fd, 0) and returns 1. With bind_test_only it closes the listening socket, calls ipc_write(ipc_fd, 1) and returns 0. For a non-SOCK_STREAM type it calls ipc_write(ipc_fd, 1), returns msg_loop(0, lsd, addr, alen, args) after closing the listening socket. For SOCK_STREAM: if args->password is set and tcp_md5_remote fails it closes the listening socket and goes to err_exit (returns 1); otherwise it calls ipc_write(ipc_fd, 1) and loops on select() with the listening socket. The loop ends with close(lsd) and return of rc in these cases: select returns 0 (rc = 2); select fails with errno other than EINTR (EINTR retries; rc is select's negative return); accept fails (rc is select's positive return value); show_sockstat or check_device returns nonzero (rc is that value, and the accepted socket csd is not closed on these two paths); or msg_loop has run on the accepted socket, csd was closed, and interactive is false (rc is msg_loop's return value). When interactive is set the loop repeats after every msg_loop call whatever its return value, so it returns only through the other exits. Every exit from the stream loop closes the listening socket; the accepted socket is closed only after msg_loop.
note: Reviewers: original (csd not closed on show_sockstat/check_device failure; select/accept returns omitted) right (nettest.c:1644-1650); round 2 (accept failure returns select's positive rc, not -1) right (lines 1638-1641, rc still holds select's return); round 15 (interactive loop repeats after any msg_loop return, not only successful) right (lines 1653-1657); the old prose said 'successful msg_loop'. Tally 3 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(proc_net_pktgen, ctrl_cmd)
prose: Test body (proc_net_pktgen.c:161-181) using the fixture's ctrl_fd, which the fixture setup opened on /proc/net/pktgen/pgctrl. It writes "stop", "start" and "reset" to ctrl_fd, each twice: once with sizeof(string) bytes (including the NUL) and once with sizeof(string) - 1 bytes. After each write it expects (EXPECT_EQ) the returned length to equal the number of bytes written. A mismatch is recorded as a non-fatal failure and the test continues with the next write, so the function returns normally after the sixth write, and the test fails if any expectation was violated.
note: Name is the TEST_F invocation. No reviewer claim; prior prose checked and kept.

name: TEST_F(proc_net_pktgen, wrong_thr_cmd)

For each i from 0 through sizeof(wrong_thr_cmd) inclusive (wrong_thr_cmd is "forsureawrongcommand"), it writes the first i bytes of wrong_thr_cmd to thr_fd and expects the write to return -1 and errno to equal EINVAL. name: build_packet
prose: Static function build_packet(payload_len) in psock_snd.c (lines 153-168) builds a test frame in the global tbuf and returns its length. It appends in order: build_vnet_header (sizeof(struct virtio_net_hdr), 10 bytes, with csum and GSO fields set from cfg_use_csum_off, cfg_use_csum_off_bad and cfg_use_gso; flags are OR-ed in, not cleared), build_eth_header (ETH_HLEN, or ETH_HLEN + 4 with a VLAN tag when cfg_use_vlan), build_ipv4_header (20 bytes, with tot_len from payload_len) and build_udp_header (8 bytes), so off is 52 bytes without VLAN and 56 with VLAN. It then checks off + payload_len > sizeof(tbuf) (the comparison is done as size_t); if true it calls error(1, 0, "payload length exceeds max"), which exits the process. Otherwise it fills tbuf + off with payload_len bytes of DATA_CHAR and returns off + payload_len, that is payload_len + 52 or payload_len + 56 with VLAN. tbuf is sizeof(struct virtio_net_hdr) + ETH_HLEN + ETH_MAX_MTU + 1 bytes (65560), so payload_len up to 65508 (65504 with VLAN) is accepted. The headers are written into tbuf before the length check. Negative payload_len is outside the intended domain: if off + payload_len is negative, the size_t comparison makes error() fire; for payload_len between -off and -1 the check passes and memset receives payload_len converted to a huge size_t.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (non-VLAN 65505-65508 returns, negative lengths do not abort) right (psock_snd.c:162-167); round 2 (formal requires payload_len <= 1481) wrong/moot, that contract is removed; round 15 (returned length is payload_len + 54/58, bounds off by two) wrong: virtio_net_hdr is 10 bytes (flags, gso_type, hdr_len, gso_size, csum_start, csum_offset), plus 14 + 20 + 8 = 52, VLAN +4 = 56 (psock_snd.c:76-151). Contract dropped because the function writes the global tbuf and reads cfg_* globals. Tally 1 right 1 wrong (1 moot).

name: main
prose: Test program entry point of reuseport_bpf.c (lines 458-639); main takes no parameters and ignores the command line. It prints section headers to stderr and runs these scenarios in order, each as a call with a struct test_params: IPv4 UDP: test_reuseport_ebpf with 10 and with 20 receive sockets, test_reuseport_cbpf with 10 and with 20, test_extra_filter, test_filter_no_reuseport; IPv6 UDP: the same six calls; IPv6 UDP with mapped IPv4 (recv AF_INET6, send AF_INET): test_reuseport_ebpf with 20 and 10 sockets and test_reuseport_cbpf with 10 and 20 sockets only; then enable_fastopen() (which may write the tcp_fastopen sysctl and calls error(1, ...) if it cannot open, read or write it); IPv4 TCP: ebpf (10), cbpf (10), test_extra_filter, test_filter_no_reuseport; IPv6 TCP: the same four; IPv6 TCP with mapped IPv4: ebpf (10) and cbpf (10) only; finally test_filter_without_bind(), prints "SUCCESS" to stderr and returns 0. The helpers return void and report failures by calling error(1, ...) (which exits with status 1), so main has no failing return path of its own; main returns 0 only when it reaches the end. A constructor and destructor outside main raise and restore RLIMIT_MEMLOCK around the whole program.
note: Slice cut the head; main is at reuseport_bpf.c:458. Reviewer round 15 (the formal contract only ensures result == 0 and omits side effects) right as a criticism of the old contract; contract removed since the function does I/O on stderr, sysctl files and sockets. The old prose said it ran 'every' scenario; extra_filter and no_reuseport tests are not run for the mapped-IPv4 sections (lines 539-567, 619-633). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: sk_peek_offset_test
prose: Static function sk_peek_offset_test(af, proto) in sk_so_peek_off.c (lines 57-168) returns 1 when every step passes and 0 otherwise (the only assignment of res = 1 is at line 159, after all checks). It creates two sockets s[0] and s[1] (SOCK_STREAM for IPPROTO_TCP, SOCK_DGRAM otherwise) with recv_sock initially equal to s[0], binds s[0] to a zeroed sockaddr of family af (wildcard address, port 0) with sizeof(union) as the length, reads the address back with getsockname, calls listen(s[0], 0) for TCP, connects s[1] to the address, and for TCP sets recv_sock = accept(s[0], NULL, NULL), treating a result <= 0 as failure. Then, on recv_sock: SO_PEEK_OFF read must be -1; after setting it to 0 (a failed setsockopt is only reported with ksft_perror) the read must be 0; send(s[1], "ab", 2) must return 2; recv(recv_sock, buf, 1, MSG_PEEK) must return 1 with 'a' and the offset must read 1; recv(buf, 2, MSG_PEEK) must return 1 with 'b' and the offset must read 2; recv(buf, 2, MSG_TRUNC) must return 2 and the offset must read 0. Each failed step prints with ksft_perror and jumps to out, returning 0. Note sk_peek_offset_get ignores a getsockopt failure (after ksft_perror) and returns an uninitialised int, so a failed read could by chance match the expected value. Cleanup at out: for TCP and recv_sock >= 0 it closes recv_sock; then closes s[1] if >= 0 and s[0] if >= 0. Consequences: on early failures after the sockets were created but before a successful accept, recv_sock is still the same descriptor as s[0], so for TCP s[0] is closed twice; and when accept returns 0 the failure path closes descriptor 0. A successful path prints a message with printf and returns 1.
note: Reviewers: round 2 (cleanup double-closes s[0] on early TCP failures; accept returning 0 treated as failure) right (sk_so_peek_off.c:75, 99-103, 161-166); round 15 (sk_peek_offset_get ignores getsockopt failure and returns an uninitialised value) right (lines 47-55). The old prose had both facts in a long sentence; rewritten with the exact conditions. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: try_accept
prose: Static function try_accept(tst_name, port, md5_addr, md5_prefix, ao_addr, ao_prefix, set_ao_required, sndid, rcvid, vrf, cnt_name, cnt_expected, needs_tcp_md5, inj) in tcp_ao/unsigned-md5.c (lines 37-121); it returns nothing, and vrf is unused. If needs_tcp_md5 is nonzero and should_skip_test(tst_name, KCONFIG_TCP_MD5) is true it returns immediately, before creating a socket and before any synchronize_threads call. Otherwise it creates a listening socket with test_listen_socket(this_ip_addr, port, 1) and, if given, installs an MD5 key for md5_addr/md5_prefix (test_set_md5), an AO key for ao_addr/ao_prefix (test_add_key) and the AO-required flag (test_set_ao_flags); each of these failing, or test_get_tcp_counters failing, calls test_error. If cnt_name is set it reads the netstat counter before; if ao_addr is set it reads the TCP counters into cnt1. It calls synchronize_threads, then test_skpair_wait_poll(lsk, 0, poll_cnt, &sk_pair) where poll_cnt is 0 when cnt_expected is TEST_CNT_GOOD and cnt_expected otherwise, then synchronize_threads again. A result of -ETIMEDOUT stores it in sk_pair and calls test_fail unless inj == FAULT_TIMEOUT; -EKEYREJECTED calls test_fail unless inj == FAULT_KEYREJECT; any other negative result calls test_error; on success it calls test_fail if inj == FAULT_TIMEOUT, then accept()s (a failed accept calls test_error; a successful one with inj == FAULT_TIMEOUT calls test_fail). inj is compared for equality with a single fault value, not tested as a bit mask. It then reads the TCP counters again into cnt2 when ao_addr is set and closes the listening socket. If cnt_name is NULL it reports test_ok ("no counter checks") and skips the counter checks, including the AO counter assertion. Otherwise it reports test_fail when the netstat counter did not increase (after <= before) and test_ok when it did, and, when ao_addr is set, calls test_assert_counters(tst_name, &cnt1, &cnt2, cnt_expected). Finally it calls synchronize_threads once more and, if an accepted socket exists (sk >= 0), test_kill_sk(sk). The netstat counter is only compared for an increase; the expected count cnt_expected is used only for the poll and the AO counter assertion.
note: Reviewers: original (FAULT_KEYREJECT success is not failed; counter only checked for increase) right on both points (unsigned-md5.c:78-80, 107-113); round 15 (AO counter assertion is skipped when cnt_name is NULL) right (lines 100-103, 114-115); the old prose said 'fault bit', but the code compares with == (line 6). Tally 3 right 0 wrong.

name: main
prose: Entry point main(argc, argv) of tcp_mmap.c (lines 445-616). getopt parses "46p:svr:w:H:zxkP:M:C:a:i": -4/-6 set cfg_family and cfg_alen, -p port, -H host, -s server flag, -r/-w rcvbuf/sndbuf, -z zerocopy, -M mss, -x hash flag, -k keepflag, -P max pacing rate, -C chunk_size, -a map_align, -i integrity; any other result (including -v, which is in the option string but has no case, and unknown options) hits the default case and calls exit(1). If map_align is 0 it uses default_huge_page_size(), or 2 MiB if that returns 0. With -s it creates a listening socket (socket failure exits 1; SO_REUSEADDR failure is ignored), calls setup_sockaddr, optionally sets TCP_MAXSEG (failure exits 1), binds and listens with backlog 128 (failure exits 1), and calls do_accept, which loops forever accepting connections and starting threads, so main does not return in server mode. Client mode: mmap_large_buffer(chunk_size, &buffer_sz) (failure exits 1), creates a socket (failure exits 1), applies buffer sizes, setup_sockaddr, optional TCP_MAXSEG (failure exits 1), connect (failure exits 1); a failing SO_MAX_PACING_RATE setsockopt only calls perror, and a failing SO_ZEROCOPY setsockopt prints and sets zflg to 0 (neither exits). With -i it fills the buffer with random data, EVP_MD_CTX_new failure prints and exits 1, then initialises SHA-256. It then sends chunks with send() (MSG_ZEROCOPY if zflg) in a loop until FILE_SZ (1 << 35) bytes have been sent or a send returns <= 0, updating the digest per chunk; if integrity is on and total == FILE_SZ it sends the SHA-256 digest. It frees the EVP context if one exists, closes the socket, unmaps the buffer and returns 0 (also after a short or failed send).
note: Slice cut the head; main starts at tcp_mmap.c:445. Reviewer round 15 (SO_MAX_PACING_RATE and SO_ZEROCOPY setsockopt failures only perror, not exit(1)) right (lines 573-582); the old prose's blanket 'any ... setsockopt failure ... exit(1)' was wrong for these two, and for the ignored SO_REUSEADDR. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(tls, recv_partial)
prose: Test body (tls.c:1104-1122) using the tls fixture's connected pair (fd sends, cfd receives). It builds the string "test_read_partial" (17 characters) and sends strlen + 1 = 18 bytes, including the NUL, with send(self->fd, ...), expecting the return value 18. It then calls recv(self->cfd, recv_mem, 9, MSG_WAITALL), expecting 9 and the bytes "test_read"; clears recv_mem, calls recv(self->cfd, recv_mem, 8, MSG_WAITALL), expecting 8 and the bytes "_partial". The NUL byte is left unread. All checks are non-fatal EXPECT_EQ expectations; the body returns nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 (send length is strlen + 1 = 18, not 17) right (tls.c:1109, 1113); the old prose said 17. The slice cut the head, name fixed to the real TEST_F. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(tls, rekey_fail)
prose: Test body (tls.c:1985-2057; the slice began at line 2036, in the middle of it, so no function named tls_rekey_recv exists). It sends and receives test_message_before_rekey on the pair, then sends a TLS KeyUpdate with tls_send_keyupdate on fd. If the variant's tls_version is not TLS 1.3 it only checks that setsockopt(TLS_TX) on fd fails with -1 and errno EBUSY and returns. For TLS 1.3 it checks a valid TX rekey succeeds (0), then that three invalid updates fail with -1 and errno EINVAL (a TX update with a changed version, an RX update on cfd with a changed version, a TX update with a changed cipher), sends test_message_after_rekey (expecting the full length), and expects recv on cfd without a control message to return -1 (errno not checked). After tls_recv_keyupdate on cfd it expects recv to return -1 with errno EKEYEXPIRED, both blocking and with MSG_DONTWAIT; it installs a new RX key with setsockopt(TLS_RX) on cfd (expecting 0), and expects the next recv to return something other than -1 (EXPECT_NE) with the data equal to test_message_after_rekey. All checks are non-fatal EXPECT_* expectations.
note: Slice cut the head; the old prose described the tail of this test (and said recv returns send_len, but the code only expects not -1, tls.c:2055). No reviewer claim beyond mechanical rejection.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, timeo)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2744-2774) for the tls_err fixture. If self->notls is set it skips with SKIP(return, ...). Otherwise it sets SO_RCVTIMEO of 10 ms on self->cfd2 (ASSERT_EQ on the setsockopt result) and forks (ASSERT_GE on the fork result). The parent sleeps 1 ms, then calls recv(cfd2, buf, 128, 0) twice, expecting -1 with errno EAGAIN each time, and calls wait(); it does not check the child's status. The child calls recv(cfd2, ...) once, expecting -1 with EAGAIN, and then exit(0).
note: Reviewer round 15 (the child performs only one recv) right (tls.c:2770-2772). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, poll_partial_rec)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2776-2808; the slice began at 2790 and cut the head). It skips when self->notls is set. It polls self->cfd2 for POLLIN with a 1 ms timeout, expecting 0 events. It sends 128 random bytes on self->fd, reads the resulting TLS record from self->cfd into a 256-byte buffer (expecting a length greater than 128), sends the first 100 bytes of the record on self->fd2 (expecting 100), polls cfd2 again for 1 ms expecting 0, sends the remaining rec_len - 100 bytes, polls expecting 1, then recv(cfd2, rec, 256, 0) is expected to return 128 and the data to equal the 128 bytes sent. All are non-fatal EXPECT_* expectations.
note: Old record was dropped because the slice cut the head; the test exists at tls.c:2776 so it is fixed under the real name.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, epoll_partial_rec)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2810-2847). It skips when self->notls is set. It creates an epoll instance and adds self->cfd2 for EPOLLIN (ASSERT_GE on both calls), and expects epoll_wait(..., timeout 0) to return 0. It sends 128 random bytes on self->fd, reads the TLS record from self->cfd (length expected greater than 128), sends the first 100 bytes of the record on self->fd2 (expecting 100), and expects epoll_wait with timeout 0 to return 0; it sends the remaining bytes, expects epoll_wait to return 1, then expects recv(cfd2, rec, 256, 0) to return 128 with the data equal to the 128 bytes sent, and closes the epoll fd. The ASSERTs end the test on failure (without closing epollfd); the EXPECTs do not.
note: Prior prose checked against tls.c:2810-2847; it omitted the initial empty epoll_wait and used 'exactly one event' loosely (the check is return value 1). No reviewer claim.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, poll_partial_rec_async)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2849-2904). It skips when self->notls is set, creates a pipe (ASSERT_GE), sends 128 random bytes on self->fd, reads the TLS record from self->cfd (expecting more than 128 bytes), and forks (ASSERT_GE). Parent: closes p[1], sleeps 1 ms, sends the first 100 bytes of the record on self->fd2 (expecting 100), blocks reading one byte from p[0] (barrier, expecting 1), sends the remaining bytes, then wait()s and expects the returned pid to equal the child's pid and the status to be 0. Child: closes p[0], polls self->cfd2 for POLLIN with a 20 ms timeout expecting 0, writes one byte to p[1] (expecting 1), polls cfd2 again with a 20 ms timeout expecting 1, and exits with status !__test_passed(_metadata), so a failed expectation in the child makes the parent's status check fail. All checks are non-fatal EXPECT_* except the ASSERTs.
note: Prior prose checked against tls.c:2849-2904; clarified the child exit status and the barrier. No reviewer claim.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, oob_pressure)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2909-2920) for the tls_err fixture; it does not check self->notls. It fills a 64 KiB buffer with random bytes, sends 5 bytes with MSG_OOB on self->fd2 (expecting 5), sends the whole 64 KiB with flags 0 (expecting 65536), then sends 5 bytes with MSG_OOB on self->fd2 64 times, expecting 5 each time. The source comment says the large send after OOB is meant to trigger copy mode due to memory pressure; the test itself only checks the returned byte counts, via non-fatal EXPECT_EQ.
note: Prior prose checked; made the 'exercising the copy path' claim an intent from the source comment (tls.c:2906-2908), since the test only asserts return values. No reviewer claim.

name: run_printf
prose: Static function run_printf(min, max) in nolibc-test.c (lines 1687-1723). It loops test from min while test >= 0 and test <= max, with ret starting at 0 and a per-iteration line length llen. The switch is on test + __LINE__ + 1, so each CASE_TEST(name) labels one test by source line; a test number with no case does nothing (there is no default), and the case that is last in the switch executes return ret. For a matching case, CASE_TEST prints "<test> <name>" to stdout and then either EXPECT_VFPRINTF adds expect_vfprintf(...) to ret, or EXPECT_ZR(1, expr) adds expect_zr(expr, llen), which is 1 when the test function (test_scanf, test_strerror, test_printf_error) returns nonzero and 0 otherwise (the cond argument is the constant 1, so those cases are never skipped). expect_vfprintf formats with vsnprintf into a buffer limited to 21 bytes and returns 1 if the returned length differs from the expected count c, otherwise strncmp(expected, buf, c) (any sign, 0 on equal), printing the result to stdout. The function returns ret after the loop or at the sentinel case, so it returns 0 when no case ran or every executed case matched, and otherwise the accumulated sum, which can in principle be negative or cancel out because strncmp results can be negative.
note: Reviewers: original (negative strncmp result makes ret possibly negative) right (nolibc-test.c:1575-1578); round 2 (omits EXPECT_ZR contributions from scanf/strerror/printf_error) right (lines 1714-1716); both were already reflected in the old prose, rewritten with exact conditions. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(pcie_ep_doorbell, DOORBELL_TEST)
prose: Test body (pci_endpoint_test.c:254-263) for the pcie_ep_doorbell fixture, whose setup opens test_device ("/dev/pci-endpoint-test.0") O_RDWR into self->fd (ASSERT_NE against -1). The body uses the pci_ep_ioctl macro, which stores ioctl(self->fd, cmd, arg) in ret and replaces a negative result by -errno. It calls pci_ep_ioctl(PCITEST_SET_IRQTYPE, PCITEST_IRQ_TYPE_AUTO) and asserts ret == 0 (fatal ASSERT_EQ), then pci_ep_ioctl(PCITEST_DOORBELL, 0) and expects ret to be 0 (non-fatal EXPECT_FALSE(ret)), so any nonzero return fails the expectation. Nothing is returned.

name: TEST_F(file_handle, pid_has_exited)
prose: Test body (pidfd_file_handle_test.c:274-307) for the file_handle fixture; self->pidfd is a pidfd of the test process and self->child_pidfd3/child_pid3 a child created with CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID. It allocates a struct file_handle with MAX_HANDLE_SZ bytes of handle space (ASSERT_NE), obtains the handle of child_pidfd3 with name_to_handle_at(AT_EMPTY_PATH), fstat()s child_pidfd3, opens the handle with open_by_handle_at(self->pidfd, fh, 0) and asserts the opened pidfd has the same st_dev and st_ino, then closes it. It moves child_pidfd3 out of the fixture (self->child_pidfd3 = -EBADF), sends SIGKILL through it, closes it, and waits with waitid(WEXITED | WNOWAIT) so the child has exited but is not reaped. It then calls open_by_handle_at again and only asserts that the result is >= 0 (no stat comparison and the descriptor is not closed), and finally reaps the child with waitid(WEXITED). Failures of the ASSERT_* macros end the test early; EXPECT_* ones do not. The file_handle buffer is not freed in this test.
note: Old prose claimed the handle buffer is freed, every pidfd is closed and st_dev/st_ino match after the child exited; none of that is in the code (no free(), the second pidfd is only asserted >= 0, pidfd_file_handle_test.c:303-304). Systematic: 'buffer is freed' claim wrong in 7 of 7 file_handle tests of this slice.

The file_handle buffer is not freed in this test.

name: FIXTURE_SETUP(current_nsset)
prose: Fixture setup (pidfd_setns_test.c:91-321) for current_nsset, running before each TEST_F with a zero-initialised self supplied by the harness. It first sets every element of nsfds[], child_nsfds1[], child_nsfds2[], child_pidfd_derived_nsfds[], child_pidfd_derived_nsfds1[] and child_pidfd_derived_nsfds2[] to -EBADF. It opens /proc/self/ns as a directory (ASSERT_GE 0), stores getpid() in self->pid and a pidfd of it in self->pidfd, and for each namespace in ns_info opens /proc/self/ns/<name> into nsfds[i] and derives child_pidfd_derived_nsfds[i] with the namespace ioctl on self->pidfd; a failed open records an EXPECT_EQ(errno, ENOENT) and a failed ioctl records EXPECT_EQ(errno, EOPNOTSUPP), and the array element then holds the negative return value (-1), not -EBADF. It creates a child with create_child(&child_pidfd_exited, 0) that unshares the user and net namespaces when the matching nsfds entry is >= 0 and exits right away, and the parent asserts waitid(WEXITED | WNOWAIT) succeeds (the exited child is waited for but not reaped). It then reopens self->pidfd (the earlier pidfd is overwritten, not closed), creates two socketpair-synchronised children child_pid1 and child_pid2, each created with CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID when both namespaces are available, otherwise with whichever of those is available, otherwise with 0; each child unshares the mount, cgroup, ipc, uts and net namespaces and switches the time namespace when the corresponding nsfds entry is >= 0 (exiting with EXIT_FAILURE if one fails), writes one byte to its socketpair and pause()s; the parent asserts it reads that byte (ASSERT_EQ, read_nointr == 1) for each child. Finally it reopens nsfds[i] (overwriting the earlier descriptors without closing them), opens /proc/<child_pid1>/ns/<name> and /proc/<child_pid2>/ns/<name> into child_nsfds1[i] and child_nsfds2[i], derives child_pidfd_derived_nsfds1[i]/2[i] from the two child pidfds, with the same EXPECT_EQ(errno, ENOENT/EOPNOTSUPP) on failure (failed entries hold -1), and closes proc_fd. Only the ASSERT_* failures abort the setup; EXPECT_* failures are recorded and execution continues.
note: Slice cut the head; fixed under real macro name. Reviewer round 15 (EXPECT failures do not abort; failed openat/ioctl leave -1, not -EBADF) right on both points (pidfd_setns_test.c:119-133, 269-317). Old prose also said the exited child was 'reaped with WNOWAIT'; WNOWAIT leaves it unreaped. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(current_nsset)

It asserts (ASSERT_EQ, ending the teardown on failure) that sending SIGKILL with sys_pidfd_send_signal to self->child_pidfd1 and then self->child_pidfd2 returns 0. For every namespace index it closes, without checking the result, each of nsfds[i], child_nsfds1[i], child_nsfds2[i], child_pidfd_derived_nsfds[i], child_pidfd_derived_nsfds1[i] and child_pidfd_derived_nsfds2[i] that is >= 0. It then closes child_pidfd1 and child_pidfd2 when they are >= 0, with EXPECT_EQ(0, close(...)) (a failure is recorded, not fatal), and asserts that waitid(P_PID, ..., WEXITED) succeeds for child_pid_exited, child_pid1 and child_pid2, which reaps all three children. It does not close self->pidfd or self->child_pidfd_exited.
note: Reviewer round 15 (child_pidfd_exited is not closed, and close uses EXPECT_EQ so failures do not abort) right (pidfd_setns_test.c:347-353); the old prose said every stored fd is closed and any failure aborts. self->pidfd is not closed either. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(pidfs_xattr, set_get_list_xattr_persistent)
prose: Test body (pidfd_xattr_test.c:97-130) for the pidfs_xattr fixture, whose child (created with CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID) exits immediately; the child is reaped in the fixture teardown. The body uses ASSERT_* only, so it stops at the first failed assertion. It sets "trusted.persistent" = "persistent value" on self->child_pidfd with fsetxattr (expects 0), reads it back with fgetxattr (expects the value length and identical bytes), and calls flistxattr, expecting a positive return and that the first name in the returned list equals "trusted.persistent" (strcmp on the list start only; it does not check that it is the only entry or the list length). It then closes the pidfd (asserted 0), sets self->child_pidfd = -EBADF, sleeps 2 seconds, reopens the pidfd with sys_pidfd_open(self->child_pid, 0) (expects >= 0) and repeats the same fgetxattr and first-entry flistxattr checks. Nothing is returned.
note: Reviewer round 15 (code only strcmp's the first entry, not that it is the sole entry) right (pidfd_xattr_test.c:113, 129). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: check_all_cpu_dscr_defaults
prose: Static function check_all_cpu_dscr_defaults(val) in dscr_sysfs_test.c (lines 30-65) returns 0 or 1. It opens CPU_PATH with opendir; if that fails it prints with perror and returns 1 (there is no precondition that the directory can be opened). For each directory entry it skips entries whose d_type does not have the DT_DIR bit, the entry named "cpuidle", entries whose name does not contain the substring "cpu", entries for which snprintf of "<CPU_PATH><name>/dscr" into a LEN_MAX buffer reports a length >= LEN_MAX, and entries whose dscr file fails access(F_OK). For each remaining file it calls check_cpu_dscr_default(file, val), which reads the file as a hexadecimal unsigned long with read_ulong and returns read_ulong's nonzero error value if that read fails, 1 (after printing both values) if the value differs from val, and 0 if equal; any nonzero result makes the function close the directory and return 1 (the exact error code is not passed on, since it is only tested for truth). After all entries it closes the directory and returns 0. The directory stream is closed on every path after a successful opendir.
note: Reviewers: original (contract only bounds result to 0/1) moot, no contract; round 2 (on read_ulong failure it returns 1, not read_ulong's error code) right (dscr_sysfs_test.c:58-61); round 15 (precondition says CPU_PATH can be opened yet opendir failure is a return path; snprintf-overflow skip omitted) right on both (lines 36-40, 52-54). Tally 3 right 0 wrong (1 moot).

name: main
prose: Test program entry point (cmsg_sender.c:470-583); the packet slice cut the head, so the function is main, not send_packets. Parameters argc and argv are handed to cs_parse_args, which fills the global opt (cs_parse_args can exit the process on bad arguments). It then malloc()s opt.size bytes (the result is not checked) and fills them with memrnd, resolves opt.host/opt.service with getaddrinfo (hints.ai_family = opt.sock.family), and, if the result is AF_INET6 and the protocol is IPPROTO_ICMP, switches opt.sock.proto to IPPROTO_ICMPV6. It opens a socket(ai_family, opt.sock.type, opt.sock.proto). For ICMP/ICMPv6 it sets buf[0] to the echo-request type and buf[1] to 0; for another protocol on a SOCK_RAW socket it copies a udphdr built from {1, 2, htons(opt.size), 0} into buf and overwrites the sin6_port of ai_addr (cast to sockaddr_in6) with htons(opt.sock.proto). It then calls ca_set_sockopts(fd), reads CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC (a failure calls error(ERN_GETTIME, ...), which terminates the process), builds one iovec/msghdr addressed to ai_addr, calls cs_write_cmsg, and loops opt.num_pkt times calling sendmsg (MSG_MORE if opt.msg_more). Return values: ERN_SOCK_CREATE if getaddrinfo fails (jumping to err_free_buff, so only buf is freed; note the code uses ERN_SOCK_CREATE for the resolve failure and ERN_RESOLVE for the socket failure); ERN_RESOLVE if socket() fails (freeaddrinfo and free, no close); ERN_SEND if sendmsg returns a negative value; ERN_SEND_SHORT if sendmsg returns a value different from (int)opt.size; ERN_SEND_MORE if the follow-up write(fd, NULL, 0) returns a negative value (all three close fd, then free ai and buf); otherwise ERN_SUCCESS (0), after an optional loop of up to 40 iterations of cs_read_cmsg (stopping early when the SCM_TSTAMP_SND bit is seen, else usleep(opt.txtime.delay / 20)) when opt.ts.ena is set, then close, freeaddrinfo, free. Not covered: the malloc result is not checked, and cs_parse_args, ca_set_sockopts, cs_write_cmsg and cs_read_cmsg can end the process through error().
note: Slice cut the head; function is main at cmsg_sender.c:470 (the old prose called it send_packets and said clock_gettime failure never returned, which holds, but the ERN code mapping of the two early failures is swapped relative to their names: lines 494 and 504). No reviewer claim to check (mechanical rejection only).

name: TEST_F(epoll_busy_poll, test_set_invalid)
prose: Test body (epoll_busy_poll.c:166-267; the slice started at line 255 and showed only its tail, so test_invalid_params is not a separate function). It uses the fixture's epoll fd, params struct and capability state, and records non-fatal EXPECT_* failures rather than aborting. Steps in order: (1) zero self->params, set __pad = 1, ioctl(fd, EPIOCSPARAMS, &params) and expect -1 with errno EINVAL; (2) __pad = 0, busy_poll_usecs = (uint32_t)INT_MAX + 1, expect -1 / EINVAL; (3) busy_poll_usecs = 32, prefer_busy_poll = 2, expect -1 / EINVAL; (4) prefer_busy_poll = 1, busy_poll_budget = UINT16_MAX, check via cap_get_flag that CAP_NET_ADMIN is effective, then expect the ioctl to return 0; (5) clear CAP_NET_ADMIN from the effective set with cap_set_flag and cap_set_proc and expect the same ioctl to return -1 with errno EPERM; (6) restore the capability the same way, then call ioctl(fd, EPIOCSPARAMS, (struct epoll_params *)0xdeadbeef) and expect -1 with errno EFAULT. The function returns nothing; what the kernel returns is asserted by the test, not guaranteed by it.
note: Slice cut the head; fixed under the real test name. Old prose described only the last ioctl.

prose: Test body (epoll_busy_poll.c:269-304). It zeroes self->params, sets busy_poll_usecs = 25, busy_poll_budget = 16, prefer_busy_poll = 1 and expects ioctl(fd, EPIOCSPARAMS, &params) to return 0. It then zeroes the struct again, calls ioctl(fd, EPIOCGPARAMS, &params), expects return 0 and expects the struct to hold busy_poll_usecs 25, busy_poll_budget 16, prefer_busy_poll 1 and __pad 0. The checks are non-fatal EXPECT_* macros, so the test continues after a failed expectation; nothing is returned. The test does not itself set up capabilities (the fixture does).

It calls ioctl(self->fd, EPIOCGPARAMS + 10, &self->params), where EPIOCGPARAMS + 10 is a request number the epoll driver is not expected to handle, expects the return value -1 and expects errno to be EINVAL. name: add_standard_tcp_options
prose: add_standard_tcp_options(buf, no_ext, ts, order) (gro.c:484-512) writes TCP option bytes after the base header and then calls recompute_packet(buf, no_ext, TCPOLEN_TSTAMP_APPA) (that constant comes from the system netinet/tcp.h, where it is TCPOLEN_TIMESTAMP + 2 = 12; the header is not in this repository, so the 12 is assumed). Writes depend on order, relative to buf + total_hdr_len: order 0 writes NOP at +0, NOP at +1 and a timestamp option at +2; order 1 writes NOP at +0, timestamp at +1 and NOP at +11; order 2 writes timestamp at +0, NOP at +11 and NOP at +12. Any other order calls error(1, 0, "unknown order"), which terminates the process, and recompute_packet is not reached. tcp_write_options for the timestamp kind memsets sizeof(struct tcp_option_ts) bytes (the struct is uint8 kind, uint8 len, uint32 tsval, uint32 tsecr, so with normal alignment 12 bytes, not the 10 of TCPOLEN_TIMESTAMP), sets kind, len = TCPOLEN_TIMESTAMP, tsval = ts and tsecr = 0, so the byte at +10 in order 2 is cleared by that memset rather than left as is, and tsval is stored at struct offset 4 under that layout. recompute_packet then copies the first total_hdr_len bytes of no_ext over buf, moves PAYLOAD_LEN bytes from no_ext + total_hdr_len to buf + total_hdr_len + 12 (so any option-area byte at +12 or beyond, namely the order 2 NOP at +12 and the end of the timestamp memset area in orders 0 and 1, is overwritten by the payload), adds 12/4 to tcphdr->doff, zeroes and recomputes the TCP checksum over PAYLOAD_LEN + 12 bytes, and for PF_INET adds 12 to iph->tot_len and recomputes the IPv4 header checksum (also for the second IPv4 header when ipip is set), while for other protocols it adds 12 only to the outer IPv6 payload_len. Buffer requirement: buf must be writable at least up to total_hdr_len + 14 bytes for order 0 (timestamp memset ends at +13), total_hdr_len + 13 for orders 1 and 2, and up to total_hdr_len + 12 + PAYLOAD_LEN for the payload move; no_ext must hold total_hdr_len + PAYLOAD_LEN bytes.
note: Reviewer 1 (order 2 writes NOPs at 11 and 12, offset 10 unwritten) is mixed: NOPs are at +11 and +12 (gro.c:502-505) but the TS memset of sizeof(struct tcp_option_ts) (gro.c:469, 12 bytes with padding) zeroes +10, and the layout is still TS, NOP, NOP. Reviewer 2 (buffer minimum understated, writes past total_hdr_len+12) is right (order 0 reaches +13, orders 1/2 reach +12). Tally 1 right 0 wrong, 1 mixed.
